attempts.label: DANDI:000404
attempts.entry_title: Invariant neural dynamics in a monkey cursor BMI (Athalye et al. 2023)
attempts.description: Tests the findings of Athalye, Khanna, Gowda, Orsborn, Costa and Carmena (2023) on dandiset 000404, which holds the binned spike counts, decoder state, cursor and trials of 9 sessions of Monkey G and 4 of Monkey J in a center-out and an obstacle-avoidance BMI task. It recovers the decoder from the files, compares activity issuing the same command across conditions with behavior-preserving shuffles, fits linear dynamics models that predict that activity and the next command, and simulates the optimal feedback control model of Figure 6 on the fitted dynamics. The rsLDS comparison was not run, as its package cannot be installed in a locked environment.

outcomes.source: Results, BMI to study neural population control of movement, paragraph beginning "To study control of diverse movements"; Methods, Neuroprosthetic tasks

Reading (b), conditions with a tuple of 15 or more occurrences, gives 16.23. Monkey J's 31 obstacle trials of the code's types 0 and 1 are left out.
deviations: Targets are read from the cursor position at reward, as the files' target series do not give the trial's target (see findings); obstacle trials are labelled clockwise or counterclockwise by the code's rule (util_fcns.CW_CCW_obs), with the code's fixed labels for Monkey J types 3, 4, 5, 8 and 9.

outcomes.statement: Each analysed command was used regularly (15 or more times) in several conditions, about 7 on average, typically 5 to 10.
outcomes.source: Results, BMI to study neural population control of movement, paragraph beginning "Importantly, the BMI enabled us"; Figure S1B; Methods, Conditions that used a command regularly

outcomes.notes: Measured under the behavior-preserving shuffle, commands with two or more conditions, neurons over all tuples. Every combination of readings puts three or four of the six fractions within tolerance, none all six. outcomes.source: Figure 4C legend; Results, Invariant dynamics predict the different neural activity patterns used to issue the same command, paragraph beginning "On the level of single time points"; Table S1 (rows 4C)
outcomes.quote: Full dynamics, command left-out dynamics, and condition left-out dynamics all predicted neural activity significantly better than shuffle dynamics. For each model: Monkey G [J]: p-value < 0.001 for 9/9 [4/4] sessions, p-value < 0.001 for sessions pooled.

outcomes.notes: Scored as the code scores it, R2 is 0.1655 and 0.2492 (full), 0.1624 and 0.2418 (command left out), 0.1631 and 0.2391 (condition left out), all within 10%, each beating the shuffle scored on the same pairs with p < 0.001 in 9 of 9 and 4 of 4 sessions and pooled. The shuffle's pooled 95th percentiles, 0.1282 and 0.1963, match Table S1's 0.130 and 0.196. On pairs whose command at t is analysed the tests are the same and the values within tolerance (full 0.1705 and 0.2574). On all pairs the tests are the same, the command left-out model beating the shuffle in 9 of 9 and 4 of 4 sessions, but the full and condition left-out R2 (0.1942 and 0.2913, 0.1916 and 0.2808) are outside tolerance. As in the code (generalization_plots.predict_shuffles_v2_with_cond, one session-wide shuffle index per shuffle passed with the fold test indices), each shuffle permutes the whole session before the folds are split.

outcomes.statement: The fitted dynamics are low-dimensional, with 2 to 4 eigenvalues per session whose decay time exceeds the 0.1 s bin (2 to 5 for decoder-null dynamics), and decay to a fixed point with little rotation (mean frequency about 0.1 Hz for Monkey G and 0 Hz for Monkey J).
outcomes.source: Results, Invariant dynamics predict the different neural activity patterns used to issue the same command, paragraph beginning "We found that the dynamics were low-dimensional"; Figure S3B and S3C legends
outcomes.quote: The dimensionality of the full dynamics matrix (decoder-null dynamics matrix) ranged from 2-4 (2-5) when considering the eigenvalues that had timescales greater than the BMI update’s timescale of 0.1 seconds.
outcomes.notes: Long-timescale eigenvalues number 2 to 5 for the full model in Monkey G (5 in session 4, outside 2 to 4) and 2 to 3 in Monkey J; for decoder-null dynamics 2 to 5 in G and 1 to 4 in J (1 in session 3, outside 2 to 5). Monkey G's mean frequencies are 0.083 Hz (full) and 0.068 Hz (decoder-null), outside 0.09 to 0.11 and 0.054 to 0.066. Monkey J's long-timescale eigenvalues are real except one pair in session 0 at 0.036 Hz. Decay times are at most 0.38 s. The 99% step changes no count. Fitting the full model on rates in Hz with the same ridge grid leaves every full-model count unchanged and Monkey G's mean frequency at 0.083 Hz; the ridge fit is invariant to the scale where the grid holds the scaled parameter. That variant refits only the full model, so the decoder-null counts are not tested under it.
deviations: In-sample ridge fits on all pairs with the session's cross-validated parameter; decoder-null dynamics fit on activity projected with the recovered decoder's null space.

outcomes.statement: A recurrent switching linear dynamical system (rsLDS) does not predict neural activity better than the linear ridge dynamics model.
outcomes.source: Results, Invariant dynamics predict the different neural activity patterns used to issue the same command, paragraph beginning "We found that the dynamics were low-dimensional"; Figure S5F legend
outcomes.quote: Notably, a non-linear dynamics model (a recurrent switching linear dynamical system52) did not out-perform these simple linear dynamics
outcomes.notes: The rsLDS package the paper's code uses, ssm (github.com/lindermanlab/ssm at commit eb6c8aa33e5311d3564075807dec340759dd8081, or its only PyPI release, 0.0.1), cannot be installed in the entry's locked environment. Its setup.py imports numpy and Cython but declares no build dependencies, so `uv pip install`, which the registry uses to build the environment, fails with build isolation ('No module named Cython'). Outside the entry, with build isolation off, it installs. A timing run there, not part of the notebook, gave about 3 h of single-core compute for the criterion's design on the 4 Monkey J sessions (5 folds, K = 1 to 5, 10 Laplace-EM iterations). It gave about 35 h for Monkey G, most of it sessions 2 and 4 (110 to 115 units above 0.5 Hz). Monkey J alone would fit in two notebooks of about 20 minutes each on 4 cores if the package could be installed. Rechecked in the final revision with uv 0.13.6 at the code's commit, the build stops with 'No module named numpy'. The registry installs the lock file with a plain `uv pip install -r`, so the fix (no build isolation, or extra build dependencies in a uv configuration) is a change to the registry's tooling, not to the entry; the rsLDS comparison is left to a new attempt.

outcomes.notes: The criterion needs the point process filter's velocity update or its parameters and says the claim is blocked when the dataset has neither; the files hold neither (see findings). The notebook shows estimates in which the cursor dynamics are fitted jointly with the map, which favours the fit, so none is the criterion's test. Over all frames with the offset column in the fitted dynamics the map accounts for 98.92, 98.89, 99.57 and 99.25%; over the frames of rewarded trials 99.63, 99.63, 99.57 and 99.80% with the offset column and 99.10, 99.09, 99.09 and 99.63% without it; with the update taken as the change in velocity, 87.05 to 93.89%. The paper gives 99.6, 99.6, 99.5 and 99.8%.
deviations: Not tested. The estimated readings fit the cursor dynamics jointly with the map on the 5 ms decoder state, as the files hold no PPF parameters.

findings.statement: The files hold no decoder matrices (Kalman gain, steady-state cursor dynamics, the PPF's parameters), although the paper's Data availability lists decoder parameters among the deposited data. The code that wrote the files has these lines commented out (online_analysis/nwb_utils.py). Monkey G's steady-state gain and cursor update can be recovered exactly from the decoder state and spike counts (variance accounted for above 0.99999 on 99% of updates); Monkey J's PPF cannot, and its linear approximation must be refitted.

Monkey J's target_state and obs_details series carry one target and obstacle for every trial of a session; the writer indexes frames with the position of each go event in the event list (nwb_utils.py, targets[(go_ - start_index_overall):] with go_ an index into strobed), so the last trial's values fill the file. In Monkey G's sessions 0 and 1, checked, target_state at reward is one value for all trials and does not hold the trial's target. Targets have to be read from the cursor position at reward.

The trials table has only start and stop times. Task, target, direction around the obstacle and Monkey J's obstacle trial type are not given; the task can be read from the obstacle series of each task entry, the target from the cursor at reward, and Monkey J's obstacle trial types (the paper analyses only partial and full obstruction) only by matching start and end positions to a target list in the paper's code.

Units differ within Monkey J's files. The cursor and decoder state are in m and m/s, while target_state, obstacle_position and obs_details are stated in cm; target_state holds center-out targets in m (0.1027, 0.1384) and obstacle-task targets in cm (-3.25, 8.13) under that one unit. Monkey G's files are in cm throughout.

Question for the authors. How was Monkey J's 100 ms decoder for the simulations built (the expression for F in Methods, "BMI cursor dynamics", does not survive in the text), and in what units are the next-command errors of Table S1 (row 5E)? Here the 100 ms cursor update was fitted to the decoder state, and the errors match the paper's only when multiplied by 10.

Monkey G's decoder state does not follow the steady-state filter on 0.03 to 0.95% of updates per session, among them the first updates of each task entry, where the filter had not converged. The gain recovered on the other updates accounts for 0.928 to 1 of the variance of the velocity update over all updates, so the gain must be fitted on the updates the filter explains.

entries.name: 000404-athalye-2023
entries.title: Invariant neural dynamics in a monkey cursor BMI (Athalye et al. 2023)
entries.description: Tests the findings of Athalye, Khanna, Gowda, Orsborn, Costa and Carmena (2023) on dandiset 000404, which holds the binned spike counts, decoder state, cursor and trials of 9 sessions of Monkey G and 4 of Monkey J in a center-out and an obstacle-avoidance BMI task. It recovers the decoder from the files, compares activity issuing the same command across conditions with behavior-preserving shuffles, fits linear dynamics models that predict that activity and the next command, and simulates the optimal feedback control model of Figure 6 on the fitted dynamics. The rsLDS comparison was not run, as its package cannot be installed in a locked environment.
